label: AQ 0009
title: The line that picks the skill

questions.q: So when is it really the model?
questions.a: Partly on simple tasks: skill-creator says Claude consults skills only for tasks it can't easily handle itself, so a one-step request may never trigger one. Also when the same test set passes on one model and fails on another. Test with the model your users run.

teach.title: How it works: debugging a trigger

questions.q: Is a false alarm worse than a miss?
questions.a: Often. A miss loses some help. A false alarm puts instructions that don't fit into the agent's context, and it may follow them. For a skill with side effects, like deploying, Claude Code lets you set disable-model-invocation: true so only a person can start it.

teach.title: How it works: debugging a trigger

questions.q: How do you stop it breaking again?
questions.a: Keep the test set and rerun it whenever a description changes or a new skill arrives. A new skill with a similar description can start taking another skill's triggers.

teach.title: How it works: debugging a trigger

questions.q: Why doesn't rewriting the SKILL.md body fix a skill that fires at the wrong times?
questions.a: The agent decides from the name and description alone. It reads the body only after it has chosen, so the body can't change the choice.

questions.q: In plain words, what are recall and precision for a skill?
questions.a: Recall: of the times it should fire, how often it does. Precision: of the times it fires, how often it was right to.

questions.q: What is a near-miss prompt, and why is it the best negative test?
questions.a: A prompt that shares words with the skill but needs something else. An obviously unrelated prompt tests nothing; a near-miss shows whether the description really separates the cases.
